title: 비싸지만 맛있어요: -지만으로 좋은 점과 나쁜 점 말하기
objective: By the end, you can attach -지만 to verbs and adjectives in the present and past, and to nouns (이지만). You can also use it to join two contrasting ideas, such as a good point and a bad point, into one sentence.
summary: Learn to join two contrasting ideas into one sentence with -지만 ("but"), as in 비싸지만 맛있어요.

task.title: Use -지만 in sentences
task.line: Change the word in brackets, choose the right form, or join two ideas with -지만.

forms.when: Present. Take off -다 and add -지만. It is the same after a vowel or a consonant, and the stem never changes (어렵다 → 어렵지만).
forms.exampleMeaning: This restaurant is expensive, but the food is good.

forms.when: Past. Add -지만 after the past form (잤다 → 잤지만, 했다 → 했지만).
forms.exampleMeaning: I slept a lot yesterday, but I'm still tired.

forms.when: With a noun. After a consonant, always use 이지만. After a vowel, people often drop 이 when speaking (의사지만).
forms.exampleMeaning: It's the weekend, but I'm going to work.

watchOut: 학생지만 (X) → 학생이지만 (O): If a noun ends in a consonant, you must keep 이.
어제 비가 오지만 산에 갔어요 (X) → 어제 비가 왔지만 산에 갔어요 (O): For a past event, use the past form before -지만.
비싸 지만 (X) → 비싸지만 (O): Write -지만 right after the stem, with no space.
날씨가 좋지만 기분이 좋아요 (X) → 날씨가 좋지만 좀 추워요 (O): The two parts must contrast. Don't use -지만 for two ideas that go the same way.
exercises: Fill in the blank with 크다 + -지만: 이 가방은 ____ 가벼워요.
Fill in the blank with the past form of 하다 + -지만: 어제 친구에게 전화를 ____ 친구가 안 받았어요.
Fill in the blank with 외국 사람 + -지만: 제 친구는 ____ 한국어를 잘해요.
Choose the correct form: ① 지난주에 (바쁘지만 / 바빴지만) 운동을 했어요. ② 저는 (선생님지만 / 선생님이지만) 수학을 못해요. ③ 지금 (배고프지만 / 배고팠지만) 친구를 기다려요.
Join the two sentences into one with -지만: 한국어는 어려워요. 그런데 재미있어요.
Choose the ending that makes sense with -지만: ① 그 영화는 길었지만 (재미있었어요 / 재미없었어요). ② 우리 집은 작지만 (깨끗해요 / 좁아요).
answers: ① 바빴지만 ② 선생님이지만 ③ 배고프지만
